title: Conjecture 1.1 (r-Quasiplanar Graph Conjecture)
statement_text: The number of edges of every $r$-quasiplanar graph of $n$ vertices is $O_r(n)$.
context_text: Described as a longstanding unsolved problem in the theory of topological graphs. It has been verified for $r \leq 4$. The paper's Theorem 1.7 provides an improved upper bound for $r = 2s$, $s \geq 3$, giving at most $n\bigl(\frac{c\log n}{s}\bigr)^{2s-4}$ edges, which substantially beats the previously best known bounds of $n(\log n)^{O(\log r)}$ and $O(n(\log n)^{4r-16})$.
attributed_to: Combinatorial geometry community; see Brass, Moser, and Pach [BrMP05]
paper_contribution: Proves that every $r$-quasiplanar graph with $n \geq r$ vertices, for $r = 2s$ and $s \geq 3$, has at most $n\bigl(\frac{c\log n}{s}\bigr)^{2s-4}$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant, improving all previously known upper bounds.
notes: Header carries no parenthetical attribution, but the surrounding text explicitly labels this a longstanding open problem with reference [BrMP05]; treated as 'studies' accordingly.
paper_title: Quasiplanar Graphs, String Graphs, and the Erdos-Gallai Problem

title: Problem 1.2
statement_text: Fix an integer $r \geq 4$. Is it true that every $K_r$-free segment graph on $n$ vertices has an induced subgraph on $\Omega_r(n)$ vertices which is $K_{r-1}$-free?
context_text: A string graph (resp. segment graph) is the intersection graph of a family of continuous curves (resp. straight line segments) in the plane: vertices are the curves, adjacent when they intersect. A topological graph is $r$-quasiplanar if no $r$ of its edges pairwise cross; a longstanding conjecture states that $r$-quasiplanar graphs on $n$ vertices have $O_r(n)$ edges, known for $r\le4$ (Ackerman for $r=4$). Removing small discs around the vertices of an $r$-quasiplanar graph yields a $K_r$-free string graph on its edges; a natural approach would be to colour it with few colours so that each colour class is planar or $K_4$-free, but this fails: there are $K_3$-free segment graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number (Pawlik et al., from Burling's construction), and Krawczyk and Walczak built $K_r$-free string graphs needing $\Omega_r(\log\log n)$ colours if each class must induce a $K_{r-1}$-free graph. The question here asks for a single large $K_{r-1}$-free induced subgraph instead. Suk showed (building on McGuinness) that every $K_r$-free segment graph on $n$ vertices has a $K_{r-1}$-free induced subgraph on $\Omega_r(n/\log n)$ vertices. The authors prove that every $K_r$-free string graph on $n$ vertices has a $K_{r-1}$-free induced subgraph on $cn/\log^2 n$ vertices and use this to improve the edge bound for $r$-quasiplanar graphs; the linear bound for segment graphs remains open. They also conjecture the analogous linear bound for $K_r$-free circle graphs (where the bound $\Omega(n/\log r)$ follows from Davies' colouring result) and for intersection graphs of axis-parallel boxes.
paper_title: Quasiplanar Graphs, String Graphs, and the Erdos-Gallai Problem
